title: Gluten-Free Raspberry Lemonade Cupcakes
shortDescription: Bright gluten-free cupcakes with raspberry puree and lemon zest, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a glass of raspberry lemonade on a hot day. I tested this batch in my own kitchen three times to get the gluten-free flour ratio right, and this one holds its shape and stays moist for two days. Fresh raspberry puree goes straight into the batter, not just the frosting, so every bite has real fruit flavor. Lemon zest adds the sharp citrus note that keeps the sweetness in check. The pink swirl frosting is simple: butter, powdered sugar, a splash of lemon juice, and a spoon of raspberry puree swirled through by hand. You get a marbled pink look without any food coloring. This recipe works well for spring parties or anyone who needs a gluten-free treat that does not taste like a substitute.
ingredients: 1 3/4 cups gluten-free all-purpose flour blend (with xanthan gum)
1/2 cup fresh raspberry puree, strained of seeds
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the gluten-free flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat the softened butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Mix in vanilla and lemon zest.
Add the dry mix in two batches, alternating with the milk. Mix on low until just combined.
Fold in the raspberry puree and lemon juice by hand until the batter turns a light pink.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For frosting, beat butter until smooth. Add powdered sugar in two batches, beating on low.
Mix in lemon juice and half the raspberry puree until fluffy. Fold in the rest of the puree by hand for swirls, do not overmix.
Pipe frosting onto fully cooled cupcakes using a large open star tip for a visible swirl.
tips: Strain the raspberry puree through a fine sieve twice. Seeds left in the batter make the crumb feel gritty.
Weigh your gluten-free flour if you can. Too much flour is the top reason these cupcakes turn dense.
Fold the last bit of raspberry puree into the frosting by hand, not the mixer, so you get a marbled swirl instead of solid pink.
Bring eggs and butter to room temperature first. Cold ingredients make gluten-free batter separate.

faq.question: Can I use frozen raspberries for the puree?
faq.answer: Yes. Thaw them fully, drain the extra liquid, then blend and strain out the seeds. Frozen raspberries actually give a stronger color.

faq.question: Why did my cupcakes turn out gummy in the middle?
faq.answer: This usually means too much raspberry puree in the batter or underbaking. Stick to the 1/2 cup amount and bake until a toothpick comes out fully clean.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy-free too?
faq.answer: Swap the butter for a plant-based baking stick and the milk for almond milk. The raspberry lemon flavor holds up fine either way.

faq.question: How far ahead can I bake the cupcakes?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in a sealed container. Frost the same day you plan to serve them.

conclusion: These raspberry lemonade cupcakes bring real fruit flavor and a bright citrus edge to a gluten-free treat. I keep coming back to this recipe every spring because the batter stays soft and the frosting swirl always looks like more work than it actually is. Give it a try and let the raspberry lemon combo speak for itself.
